nodes.title: Money module: provider cost card, estimate, wallet states, IST period caps, usage statement, reconciliation; price card empty

Per-minute provider cost = catalog list prices x an explicit assumed minute profile (50% caller audio gated, 4 replies/min x 2000 in + 60 out tokens, 30 s speech at 15 chars/s, half a 60 s pulse per call)
nodes.rationale: catalog.py prices are per token/char/audio-minute; an estimate needs a usage shape, and labelling it as an assumption keeps the estimate honest
nodes.reverse_if: the meter has n>=50 real calls per stack: replace the profile with measured per-stack averages

nodes.title: The fake payment gateway is never the default; the real adapter ships disabled until the owner switches on a gateway
nodes.rationale: a fake that captures every charge credits money for nothing if it leaks into production
nodes.reverse_if: never for the fake; the real adapter is enabled when the owner approves a gateway and keys live outside the repo

nodes.title: 50 parallel reservations under one ₹1,000 cap at ₹27.92 each: exactly 35 held, 0 overrun; 50 parallel against a ₹100 wallet at ₹7: exactly 14
nodes.method: node:test, Promise.all of 50 transactions on a Postgres 16 throwaway cluster, kernel ledger.reserve

nodes.title: ledger.settle charges the actual cost even above the hold, so a cap can be overrun when a call runs past its reserved maximum
nodes.mitigation: kernel clamps the cap charge to the hold and records the excess; runtime ends calls at the reserved max duration (money STATUS needs_from_others #1; todo test proves it)
nodes.resolution: Kernel 4b8ccae: settle charges min(actual, held) and records overrun_inr_milli; the money test now asserts the cap holds.

nodes.title: What does a real connected minute use per stack (caller audio share, replies, tokens, characters)?
nodes.closes_when: the meter has cost lines from n>=50 real calls per stack and the cost card is recomputed from them
